properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Des Plaines River near Russell affecting Lake IL County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Des Plaines River from IL/WI state line downstream to US-41
in Gurnee, including the Russell gauge.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Low-lying wetlands and agricultural land is
inundated near the river.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 7.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The river continues to gradually rise. The
maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM CDT
Saturday was 7.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.4 feet
early tomorrow afternoon. The river is forecast to remain above
flood stage through at least the middle of the week.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.4
feet on 02/17/2005.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means water levels above flood stage are imminent or
may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 48 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 48 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Sunday afternoon.

shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 3 at 7:22PM EDT until October 3 at 10:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Turner County in south central Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 1015 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 722 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ashburn, Sycamore, Rebecca, Amboy, Turner Co Airport and Inaha.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Henderson County in central Texas...

* Until 900 PM CDT.

across the warned area. Between 6 and 9 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Murchison.
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Southern Hancock, Southern Harrison and Southern Jackson.

heavy rainfall are expected this evening and continuing through
Sunday. A large area with rainfall amounts of 4 to 7 inches with
locally higher amounts of 8 to 10 inches is expected in the watch
area through Sunday evening.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 3 at 10:06AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A stronger weather system is expected to move into the panhandle
Saturday into Sunday, bringing periods of moderate to heavy rain.
The peak of heavier rainfall is forecast to occur overnight Saturday
into Sunday, when rain rates could exceed 0.15 inches per hour.

Total rainfall accumulations for the event are expected to be
between 1.5 and 3.0 inches, with the greatest amounts in the central
panhandle. Upwards of 5 inches is possible for higher elevations.
Due to the abbreviated period of the heaviest rainfall, smaller
creeks and streams could rise quickly, but are not expected to flood.

In addition, this system will bring a period of gusty winds over
land Saturday night. Several wind advisories have been issued,
primarily for the coastal locations, however, wind gusts are
expected between 25-30 mph for inland areas such as Wrangell, Kake,
Ketchikan, Hoonah, Gustavus, Petersburg, and Juneau.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, At the initial flood stage of 19.5 feet,
the water level in the Lower Rio Puerco will begin to threaten
several homes and structures in the village of San Francisco
between Interstate 25 and the Rio Grande. Further rises in water
levels would begin to flood the village of San Francisco. The last
time the water level reached 19.5 feet in the Rio Puerco near
Bernardo was August 10 2006.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MDT Saturday the stage was 19.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.8 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 08/10/2006.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Fillmore, NE; York, NE
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 3 at 8:35AM CDT until October 4 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by recent excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Along the West Fork Big Blue River in Southeastern York
County in east central Nebraska and Northwestern Fillmore County in
south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 100 PM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 824 AM CDT, the gauge along the West Fork Big Blue River north
of Grafton was at 12.7 feet, which was above minor flood stage of
11.0 feet. As a result, fairly widespread flooding of pastures
and fields immediately adjacent to the river continues, including
downstream through the McCool Junction area. Based on trends at
the Grafton gauge, water levels appear to have crested and have
started a very slow, gradual drop that should continue over the
next few days. However, it now appears that the river will likely
remain above flood stage until at least sometime on Sunday,
prompting this Warning to be extended out farther in time.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
McCool Junction.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction: Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 3 at 5:30PM ChST until October 5 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Guam, Rota, Saipan and Tinian.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) is steadily moving northeast and away from
the Marianas. To the south of Choi-wan, surging monsoon inflow
will maintain wet conditions through Sunday, resulting in 3 to 5
inches of rain for Guam and Rota, and 4 to 6 inches for Tinian
and Saipan during the Watch period.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 3 at 1:57AM EDT until October 4 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 2 at 1:42PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...In Imperial County. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Oct 3 6AM to Midnight.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
